solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One male leading holy warriors

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
pi is informal British slang for pious or sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A single man at the head of a band of religious fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is crossword-familiar for holy.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a regiment of Zulu fighters, so the plural noun fits a body of soldiers.

clue.text: Political approach offering new maxims about end of war

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go around the other piece
new means the letters are given a fresh arrangement
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A political movement rolls out fresh slogans about ending conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges MAXIMS, which 'about' wraps round R, the last letter of war.
explanation.definitionFit: Marxism is a political ideology and economic theory, a political approach.

clue.text: Pointer in last pages of book?

definitions.meaning: the ... finger points, and an ... is an indicator
a book's alphabetical reference list sits at the back

explanation.surface: A clue hinting at where to look in the closing pages of a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a pointer or indicator and the alphabetical list at the back of a book.

clue.text: Sailor gets with it, drunken chum, rather unreasonable

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A seaman turns up with a tipsy friend, which is somewhat excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something going slightly too far, which is behaviour that is rather unreasonable.

clue.text: Cut tax — easy? Not entirely

indicators.note: the answer is not the entire phrase, only part of the words

explanation.surface: A question about whether reducing taxation is simple.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe is to cut, as in cutting spending or jobs.

clue.text: Goal slammed into net, in at the very start

indicators.note: the word in goes at the very beginning
slammed suggests violent impact that knocks these letters out of order

explanation.surface: A football goal smashed into the net in the opening seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goal' looks like the football event; it means aim. 'slammed' rearranges INTO NET into TENTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An intention is an aim or purpose, a synonym for goal.

clue.text: People complaining — some ran off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Grumblers, some of whom fled.
explanation.definitionFit: Moaners are people who grumble, a plural noun matching those complaining.

clue.text: Dishonest competitor caught ahead of race

indicators.note: ahead of puts the caught letter first

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a heat is a qualifying race

explanation.surface: A rule-breaking runner is caught before the race starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheat is someone who breaks the rules to win, a dishonest competitor.

clue.text: Garden — it is made awkward by this slope

indicators.note: making the letters awkward puts them out of their natural order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a hill makes their garden hard to manage.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is the degree of incline, a synonym for slope.

clue.text: Coarse person, unknown character becoming top

parts.note: an ape is a crude, uncouth person
X is the algebraic symbol for an unknown

explanation.surface: A boor of mysterious identity rises to the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or summit, a synonym for top as a noun.

clue.text: Maiden, well-favoured, wanting kiss — seductive lady

parts.note: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
to be in is to be popular or in favour
X is the conventional sign for a kiss

explanation.surface: A pretty girl who lacks a kiss is portrayed as a temptress.
explanation.definitionFit: A minx is a flirtatious, impudent young woman, so a seductive lady is a fair description.

clue.text: Settings in which prisoner is given things to read

parts.note: a con is slang for a convict
texts are written works to be read

explanation.surface: A jail where an inmate is handed reading material.
explanation.definitionFit: The surrounding circumstances in which something happens are its settings or background.

clue.text: Like the most delicious tea maybe — ice tea Mrs prepared?

definitions.text: Like the most delicious tea maybe

indicators.note: letters that are prepared are made up into a new form

explanation.surface: Mrs Somebody makes iced tea which might be the most delicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea with plenty of milk or cream is richest and smoothest, superlative to match 'the most'.

clue.text: Hold up one troublemaker needing to meet PM shortly

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous creature, one troublemaker

indicators.note: shortly means the name is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Anthony Eden was a British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: Someone delays a nuisance who has to see the Prime Minister briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold up is to delay or obstruct progress, a synonym for hinder.

clue.text: Demanding old lover on island wanting man

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a gent is a gentleman

explanation.surface: A former partner on an island wants a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means pressing or requiring much, a synonym for demanding.

clue.text: Maybe fly home with group of believers

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a sect is a religious faction

explanation.surface: A household joined by a religious community, perhaps on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' reads as a verb about travel; it is the creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly is one example of a six-legged creature, hence the 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Persuasive types, awfully coarse, cross inside

indicators.note: inside means the cross sits within the shuffled letters
awfully suggests these letters are badly mangled into another order

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Smooth talkers who are terribly crude but angry within.
explanation.definitionFit: Coaxers gently persuade others, so they are persuasive people.

clue.text: Speaker in the first half is fellow showing charm

indicators.note: only the first half of the word for a speaker is used

parts.note: a talker is someone who speaks
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A commentator during the opening half seems a charismatic chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the first half' keeps TAL from TALKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object thought to bring luck, a lucky charm.

clue.text: A sign of treasure on island in Irish sea? One assumes it is true

parts.note: X marks the spot on a treasure map
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man, which lies in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A treasure map's X on a Manx island, prompting an assumption.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a proposition accepted without proof, something assumed to be true.

clue.text: Test in English before ten in the morning

indicators.note: before places the English letter ahead of the rest

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: A paper in English sat before ten o'clock in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a formal written or oral assessment, a test.

clue.text: Outlaw formerly spotted on French island

parts.note: ex means former
ile is French for island

explanation.surface: A former bandit seen on an island off France.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlaw someone can mean to banish them, so the verb matches send away from home.

clue.text: End of line attached to equipment that can fly

indicators.note: attached to puts the last letter after the gear

parts.note: kit is a set of equipment

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A string tied to gear that is able to take to the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attached to' sets the E after KIT, and the whole clue paints the toy on its line.
explanation.definitionFit: A kite is a toy airborne on the wind, something able to take flight.

clue.text: Reclusive types as before, little people

parts.note: ere is an archaic word for before
mites are tiny creatures or small children

explanation.surface: Shy folk, as ever, are small people.
explanation.definitionFit: Eremites are hermits, people who withdraw from society.

clue.text: Aim to finish

definitions.meaning: to bring to a close or conclude

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an objective and to bring something to its conclusion.

clue.text: Copied it — made it in different format

indicators.note: putting the letters in a different format means rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone reproduced a thing by making it in another style.
explanation.definitionFit: To have imitated is to have mimicked or reproduced, the past tense matching copied.

clue.text: Irish poetry needing no introduction

indicators.note: the word for poetry loses its introduction, the opening letter

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Irish poems so famous they need no preface.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is the old name for the Gaelic language of Ireland or Scotland.
